Atlas Payments is finalizing our procurement packet for the upcoming pilot and we need the following to complete our legal review:

- Current subprocessor roster (names, location of data processing, purpose).

Maya / Jonas — forwarding the security pack. Per your request, attached are our redacted SOC 2 Type II (2024) and CAIQ/ SIG-Lite responses. A few clarifications below: 

- Onward transfers: we use a small set of subprocessors that may result in cross-border transfers (cloud providers and specialist tooling). Those vendors are listed in the CSV and include the country/region of processing. Transfers to the US are protected by SCCs where applicable; we can add Atlas to the flow-down clause in the DPA amendment.

- VectorOps (observability) — US-based, processes logs for monitoring. We do not include raw user transcripts in logging by default; tracing is metadata-only unless the customer requests transcript capture for evaluation.

- KeySafe KMS (key management) — integrates with customer-managed keys if required; otherwise keys are managed in our HSM provider in the US.

- If you have HIPAA/healthcare use cases (I saw Lumina Health on the scoping doc), we can provide a scoped DPIA and offer a BAA conversation; please confirm whether PHI will be processed.

Attachments: SOC2-report-redacted-2024.pdf (stub); CAIQ-responses-2025.pdf (stub); subprocessors_20250612_v1.csv (same roster)

Next steps: we’ll send the DPA amendment via DocuSign once Atlas confirms acceptance of the listed subprocessors and onward-transfer approach.

Thanks Neha — the materials are helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we route to our privacy team: 

1) VectorOps: is data for monitoring processed in the EU for EU tenants? Your roster shows VectorOps endpoints in the US. Can you confirm whether logs (even metadata) ever leave the EEA?

2) If Atlas were to enable transcript capture for product evaluation, would those transcripts be stored long-term by VectorOps or KeySafe? We need explicit retention and deletion commitments for any vendor that might hold transcripts.

3) For the DPA amendment: can you add the specific clause that Atlas requires for onward transfer permission (we will need Atlas to explicitly permit transfers to named subprocessors and related cloud providers)? We can accept a DocuSign amendment if it contains that clause.

Also: if PHI is in scope (Lumina Health), we will need a scoped DPIA and a BAA. Please advise whether Redwood has standard DPIA materials for that scenario.

If you can answer in-line and send the DocuSign link, we’ll aim to sign the amendment within 2 business days.

Best,
Maya

Hi Maya — thanks for the detailed questions. Quick answers inline: 

1) VectorOps: for EU customers we operate VectorOps within our EU tenant where feasible; however, in some cases observability is routed to our US-based processing with SCCs in place. We will add a note to the DPA amendment specifying that VectorOps processes EU telemetry under SCCs and we will provide the hosting region per-customer in the roster.

2) Transcript retention: Redwood does not persist raw transcripts to third-party observability vendors by default. If a customer opts into transcript capture for product evaluation, retention and deletion rules are defined in the customer configuration and flow-down terms; we will add explicit retention windows (default 30 days, configurable) to the DPA amendment. KeySafe does not store transcript content — only encryption keys/metadata when customer-managed keys are not used.

3) DPA amendment & onward-transfer clause: we have updated the DocuSign amendment to include an explicit onward-transfer permission clause that lists named subprocessors (CloudProviderOne, VectorOps, KeySafe KMS) and commits to SCCs/adequacy where required. DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/sign/ABC-Atlas-DPA-2025

4) DPIA / BAA: we can provide a scoped DPIA template for healthcare workloads and we are open to a BAA conversation. If Lumina Health is processing PHI, please confirm scope and we’ll have Security produce the DPIA within 5 business days.

Attachments: reference copies (SOC2, CAIQ) are already shared in the Drive. I’m happy to hop on a 30-min call with Atlas legal/privacy if that speeds things up — Jonas, want to propose times?

Thanks,
